content:
You can use `@gentleduck/ui` from JavaScript projects.

The source and docs are authored in TypeScript, but runtime usage works the same in JavaScript. You can copy component code and remove type annotations where needed.

## Notes for JavaScript users

* Install and use components exactly as shown in the docs.
* Ignore type-only imports and type annotations in TypeScript snippets.
* Keep your project aliases configured (`@/*` etc.) so copied component imports resolve correctly.

<Callout icon={<Lightbulb />}>
  TypeScript is recommended for better editor support and safer refactors, but it is not required to use the components.
</Callout>

## Next steps

* [Installation](/duck-ui/installation)  -  Set up your project
* [CLI](/duck-cli)  -  Add components quickly
* [Components](/duck-ui)  -  Browse available UI components

## Overview

duck-ui supports monorepo setups where UI components live in a shared package consumed by multiple apps. The CLI handles workspace detection, config placement, and component installation paths automatically.

## Typical workspace structure

```
my-monorepo/
├── apps/
│   ├── web/           # Next.js app
│   └── docs/          # Docs site
├── packages/
│   └── ui/            # Shared UI package
│       ├── src/
│       │   ├── components/
│       │   │   └── ui/
│       │   ├── hooks/
│       │   ├── libs/
│       │   └── styles.css
│       ├── duck-ui.config.json
│       ├── package.json
│       └── tsconfig.json
├── package.json
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml
└── turbo.json
```

## Initialize with the CLI

Run the init command from the monorepo root, specifying the workspace where components should be installed:

```bash
npx @gentleduck/cli init --workspace packages/ui
```

Or use the interactive prompts (without `--yes`):

```bash
npx @gentleduck/cli init
```

The CLI will detect your workspaces and prompt you to select the target package.

## Config format

The CLI generates a `duck-ui.config.json` in the workspace directory:

```json title="packages/ui/duck-ui.config.json" showLineNumbers
{
  "schema": "https://gentleduck.org/schema.json",
  "rsc": false,
  "monorepo": true,
  "workspace": {
    "root": ".",
    "project": "."
  },
  "tailwind": {
    "baseColor": "zinc",
    "css": "./src/styles.css",
    "cssVariables": true,
    "prefix": ""
  },
  "aliases": {
    "ui": "~/ui",
    "libs": "~/libs",
    "hooks": "~/hooks",
    "pages": "~/pages",
    "layouts": "~/layouts"
  }
}
```

## Adding components

Add components to the shared UI package by specifying the workspace:

```bash
npx @gentleduck/cli add button --workspace packages/ui
npx @gentleduck/cli add dialog card --workspace packages/ui
```

Components are installed relative to the workspace's configured aliases.

## CSS setup

The styles file lives in the shared UI package (e.g. `packages/ui/src/styles.css`). The CLI generates the full CSS including theme variables, `@theme inline`, base layer styles, utilities, and reduced-motion preferences.

Apps import the styles from the shared package:

```ts title="apps/web/src/main.tsx"
import '@my-org/ui/styles.css'
```

Or in Next.js:

```ts title="apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx"
import '@my-org/ui/styles.css'
```

Make sure the shared package exports the CSS file in its `package.json`:

```json title="packages/ui/package.json"
{
  "exports": {
    "./styles.css": "./src/styles.css",
    "./*": "./src/components/ui/*"
  }
}
```

## Shared UI package pattern

The shared package typically re-exports all components:

```ts title="packages/ui/src/index.ts"
export * from './components/ui/button'
export * from './components/ui/dialog'
export * from './components/ui/card'
```

Apps consume components from the package:

```tsx title="apps/web/src/app/page.tsx"
import { Button } from '@my-org/ui'
```

## Working example

The [acme template](https://github.com/gentleeduck/gentleduck/tree/master/templates/acme) is a complete working monorepo example with a shared UI package, multiple apps, and Turborepo configuration. Scaffold it directly with:

```bash
npx @gentleduck/cli init --template acme --cwd my-project
```

Or clone the repo and reference it manually as a starting point for your own monorepo setup.

Create project Start by creating a new React project using `vite`. Select the **React + TypeScript** template: ```bash npm create vite@latest ``` Add Tailwind CSS ```bash npm install tailwindcss @tailwindcss/vite ``` Replace everything in `src/index.css` with the following: ```css title="src/index.css" @import "tailwindcss"; ``` Edit tsconfig.json file The current version of Vite splits TypeScript configuration into three files, two of which need to be edited. Add the `baseUrl` and `paths` properties to the `compilerOptions` section of the `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.app.json` files: ```ts title="tsconfig.json" {11-16} showLineNumbers { "files": [], "references": [ { "path": "./tsconfig.app.json" }, { "path": "./tsconfig.node.json" } ], "compilerOptions": { "baseUrl": ".", "paths": { "@/*": ["./src/*"] } } } ``` Edit tsconfig.app.json file Add the following code to the `tsconfig.app.json` file to resolve paths, for your IDE: ```ts title="tsconfig.app.json" {4-9} showLineNumbers { "compilerOptions": { // ... "baseUrl": ".", "paths": { "@/*": [ "./src/*" ] } // ... } } ``` Update vite.config.ts Add the following code to the vite.config.ts so your app can resolve paths without error: ```bash npm install -D @types/node ``` ```typescript title="vite.config.ts" showLineNumbers {1,2,8-13} import path from "path" import tailwindcss from "@tailwindcss/vite" import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react" import { defineConfig } from "vite" // https://vite.dev/config/ export default defineConfig({ plugins: [react(), tailwindcss()], resolve: { alias: { "@": path.resolve(__dirname, "./src"), }, }, }) ``` Run the CLI Run the `@gentleduck/cli` init command to setup your project: ```bash npx @gentleduck/cli init ``` You will be asked a few questions to configure `duck-ui.config.json`. ```txt Which color would you like to use as base color? › Neutral ``` Add Components You can now start adding components to your project. ```bash npx @gentleduck/cli add button ``` The command above will add the `Button` component to your project. You can then import it like this: ```tsx showLineNumbers title="src/App.tsx" import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button" function App() { return (
) } export default App ```

Add the `baseUrl` and `paths` properties to the `compilerOptions` section of the `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.app.json` files: ```ts title="tsconfig.json" {11-16} showLineNumbers { "files": [], "references": [ { "path": "./tsconfig.app.json" }, { "path": "./tsconfig.node.json" } ], "compilerOptions": { "baseUrl": ".", "paths": { "@/*": ["./src/*"] } } } ``` Edit tsconfig.app.json file Add the following code to the `tsconfig.app.json` file to resolve paths, for your IDE: ```ts title="tsconfig.app.json" {4-9} showLineNumbers { "compilerOptions": { // ... "baseUrl": ".", "paths": { "@/*": [ "./src/*" ] } // ... } } ``` Update vite.config.ts Add the following code to the vite.config.ts so your app can resolve paths without error: ```bash npm install -D @types/node ``` ```typescript title="vite.config.ts" showLineNumbers {1,2,8-13} import path from "path" import tailwindcss from "@tailwindcss/vite" import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react" import { defineConfig } from "vite" // https://vite.dev/config/ export default defineConfig({ plugins: [react(), tailwindcss()], resolve: { alias: { "@": path.resolve(__dirname, "./src"), }, }, }) ``` Run the CLI Run the `@gentleduck/cli` init command to setup your project: ```bash npx @gentleduck/cli init ``` You will be asked a few questions to configure `duck-ui.config.json`. ```txt Which color would you like to use as base color? › Neutral ``` Add Components You can now start adding components to your project. ```bash npx @gentleduck/cli add button ``` The command above will add the `Button` component to your project. You can then import it like this: ```tsx showLineNumbers title="src/App.tsx" import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button" function App() { return (
) } export default App ```

Create project Start by creating a new TanStack Start project by following the [Build a Project from Scratch](https://tanstack.com/start/latest/docs/framework/react/build-from-scratch) guide on the TanStack Start website. **Do not add Tailwind yet. We'll install Tailwind v4 in the next step.** Add Tailwind Install `tailwindcss` and its dependencies. ```bash npm install tailwindcss @tailwindcss/postcss postcss ``` Create postcss.config.ts Create a `postcss.config.ts` file at the root of your project. ```ts title="postcss.config.ts" showLineNumbers export default { plugins: { "@tailwindcss/postcss": {}, }, } ``` Create `app/styles/app.css` Create an `app.css` file in the `app/styles` directory and import `tailwindcss` ```css title="app/styles/app.css" @import "tailwindcss" source("../"); ``` Import `app.css` ```tsx title="app/routes/__root.tsx" showLineNumbers {5,21-26} import type { ReactNode } from "react" import { createRootRoute, Outlet } from "@tanstack/react-router" import { Meta, Scripts } from "@tanstack/start" import appCss from "@/styles/app.css?url" export const Route = createRootRoute({ head: () => ({ meta: [ { charSet: "utf-8", }, { name: "viewport", content: "width=device-width, initial-scale=1", }, { title: "TanStack Start Starter", }, ], links: [ { rel: "stylesheet", href: appCss, }, ], }), component: RootComponent, }) ``` Edit tsconfig.json file Add the following code to the `tsconfig.json` file to resolve paths. ```ts title="tsconfig.json" showLineNumbers {9-12} { "compilerOptions": { "jsx": "react-jsx", "moduleResolution": "Bundler", "module": "ESNext", "target": "ES2022", "skipLibCheck": true, "strictNullChecks": true, "baseUrl": ".", "paths": { "@/*": ["./app/*"] } } } ``` Run the CLI Run the `@gentleduck/cli` init command to setup your project: ```bash npx @gentleduck/cli init ``` This will create a `duck-ui.config.json` file in the root of your project and configure CSS variables inside `app/styles/app.css`. That's it You can now start adding components to your project. ```bash npx @gentleduck/cli add button ``` The command above will add the `Button` component to your project. You can then import it like this: ```tsx title="app/routes/index.tsx" showLineNumbers {1-2,7} import { createFileRoute } from "@tanstack/react-router" import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button" export const Route = createFileRoute("/")({ component: Home, }) function Home() { return (
) } ```

<Steps>
<Step>Add Tailwind CSS</Step>

Components are styled using Tailwind CSS. You need to install Tailwind CSS in your project.

[Follow the Tailwind CSS installation instructions to get started.](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/installation)

<Step>Add dependencies</Step>

Add the following dependencies to your project:

```bash
npm install @gentleduck/variants clsx tailwind-merge lucide-react tw-animate-css
```

<Step>Configure path aliases</Step>

Configure the path aliases in your `tsconfig.json` file.

```json {3-6} title="tsconfig.json" showLineNumbers
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "baseUrl": ".",
    "paths": {
      "~/*": ["./src/*"]
    }
  }
}
```

The `~` alias is a preference. You can use other aliases if you want.

<Step>Configure styles</Step>

Any question that might be related to this project you can find here. Or you can ask it on our [GitHub repository](https://github.com/gentleeduck/gentleduck).


What makes @gentleduck/ui different from other UI libraries? 57 styled components backed by 23 headless primitives we built ourselves - not Radix. Each primitive is 1% to 67% smaller than its Radix equivalent, gzipped (Accordion: 4.7 KB vs 8.6 KB). The calendar is 9.7 KB with 4 calendar systems, against 20.0 KB for react-day-picker with 1. We also ship a keyboard command system, animation tokens, atom-based state management, and a CLI with interactive merge TUI. See the full comparison with shadcn/ui. Is @gentleduck/ui just another UI clone? No. The primitives are written from scratch, and all 23 share one set of internals (Slot, Presence, Popper, focus scope). The calendar engine supports 4 calendar systems with 7 date adapters. The variant system adds memoization over class-variance-authority. The CLI has an interactive merge TUI for updating components without losing local changes. These are not wrappers around existing libraries - they are independent implementations with the same API patterns so migration is easy. Can I migrate from my current UI library? Yes. If you are on shadcn/ui, migration is a namespace swap - same component names, same compound patterns, same Tailwind classes. Both component sets coexist in the same project. Replace one component at a time with npx @gentleduck/cli add button. If you are on Radix, the primitive imports change from @radix-ui/react-dialog to @gentleduck/primitives/dialog with the same API. See the shadcn migration guide or Radix migration guide. How do I install and get started? Run npx @gentleduck/cli init to set up your project, then npx @gentleduck/cli add button (or any component name) to install specific components. Import and use them like any other React component. Is it production ready? It's used in production. Every component is optimized for performance, accessibility, and reliability. If something doesn't work, it gets fixed ASAP. How customizable are the components? Every component supports theme customization, style overrides, and composition patterns. Want to build your own components using our primitives? Go for it. Need to fork and modify something? Do it. Nothing is locked down. What about accessibility? Accessibility is part of every component. ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, screen reader support, focus management. We follow WCAG guidelines because shipping inaccessible products in 2026 is inexcusable. Does it work with TypeScript? Full TypeScript support with type definitions for every component. Autocomplete, type checking, and IntelliSense. How can I contribute or report issues? Head to our GitHub repository at{' '} github.com/gentleeduck/gentleduck . Report bugs, request features, submit pull requests, or improve documentation. We review contributions quickly and actually respond. Good ideas get implemented, bad ideas get thoughtful explanations. No corporate bureaucracy. What's the performance like? Measured, gzipped: every primitive both libraries ship is 1% to 67% smaller than Radix's (Popover: 23.0 KB vs 23.8 KB, Toggle Group: 4.7 KB vs 8.2 KB). The calendar is 9.7 KB against react-day-picker's 20.0 KB, and the useCalendar hook alone is 5.8 KB. The variant system caches results with a Map-based memoizer so repeated cva() calls in hot render paths return instantly. The primitives, calendar and variants packages are tree-shakeable ESM with sideEffects: false. See the full benchmarks. Is there documentation and examples? Yes. Documentation, code examples, and real-world use cases. Written for developers who read docs. What's the license? MIT license. Use it for anything: personal projects, commercial products, client work. Does it support dark mode? Light, dark, and custom themes all ship in. The theming system handles dynamic switching, user preferences, and custom color schemes. Who maintains this project? @wildduck2 is the main maintainer, backed by the @gentleduck organization. Active development, responsive to community feedback, and committed long-term. Can I use this with Next.js, Remix, or other frameworks? Yes. What makes @gentleduck/ui different from other UI libraries? 57 styled components backed by 23 headless primitives we built ourselves - not Radix. Each primitive is 1% to 67% smaller than its Radix equivalent, gzipped (Accordion: 4.7 KB vs 8.6 KB). The calendar is 9.7 KB with 4 calendar systems, against 20.0 KB for react-day-picker with 1. We also ship a keyboard command system, animation tokens, atom-based state management, and a CLI with interactive merge TUI. See the full comparison with shadcn/ui. Is @gentleduck/ui just another UI clone? No. The primitives are written from scratch, and all 23 share one set of internals (Slot, Presence, Popper, focus scope). The calendar engine supports 4 calendar systems with 7 date adapters. The variant system adds memoization over class-variance-authority. The CLI has an interactive merge TUI for updating components without losing local changes. These are not wrappers around existing libraries - they are independent implementations with the same API patterns so migration is easy. Can I migrate from my current UI library? Yes. If you are on shadcn/ui, migration is a namespace swap - same component names, same compound patterns, same Tailwind classes. Both component sets coexist in the same project. Replace one component at a time with npx @gentleduck/cli add button. If you are on Radix, the primitive imports change from @radix-ui/react-dialog to @gentleduck/primitives/dialog with the same API. See the shadcn migration guide or Radix migration guide. How do I install and get started? Run npx @gentleduck/cli init to set up your project, then npx @gentleduck/cli add button (or any component name) to install specific components. Import and use them like any other React component. Is it production ready? It's used in production. Every component is optimized for performance, accessibility, and reliability. If something doesn't work, it gets fixed ASAP. How customizable are the components? Every component supports theme customization, style overrides, and composition patterns. Want to build your own components using our primitives? Go for it. Need to fork and modify something? Do it. Nothing is locked down. What about accessibility? Accessibility is part of every component. ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, screen reader support, focus management. We follow WCAG guidelines because shipping inaccessible products in 2026 is inexcusable. Does it work with TypeScript? Full TypeScript support with type definitions for every component. Autocomplete, type checking, and IntelliSense. How can I contribute or report issues? Head to our GitHub repository at{' '} github.com/gentleeduck/gentleduck . Report bugs, request features, submit pull requests, or improve documentation. We review contributions quickly and actually respond. Good ideas get implemented, bad ideas get thoughtful explanations. No corporate bureaucracy. What's the performance like? The calendar is 9.7 KB against react-day-picker's 20.0 KB, and the useCalendar hook alone is 5.8 KB. The variant system caches results with a Map-based memoizer so repeated cva() calls in hot render paths return instantly. The primitives, calendar and variants packages are tree-shakeable ESM with sideEffects: false. See the full benchmarks. Is there documentation and examples? Yes. Documentation, code examples, and real-world use cases. Written for developers who read docs. What's the license? MIT license. Use it for anything: personal projects, commercial products, client work. Does it support dark mode? Light, dark, and custom themes all ship in. Active development, responsive to community feedback, and committed long-term. Can I use this with Next.js, Remix, or other frameworks? Yes. We ship installation guides for Next.js, Vite, React Router, Astro, Laravel, TanStack Start, and manual setup. The CLI auto-detects your project type. React 18+ required.

## What is Duck UI?

Duck UI is a component library built on [gentleduck primitives](/duck-primitives). The primitives are headless and accessible; Duck UI adds Tailwind styles and sensible defaults.

Part of the [gentleduck/ui](https://github.com/gentleeduck/gentleduck) ecosystem, alongside
`duck-vim`, `duck-calendar`, `duck-primitives`, and the rest of the toolchain.

## Why Duck UI

* **Built on gentleduck primitives**: No Radix dependency. Full control of every behavior.
* **Accessible defaults**: ARIA, keyboard navigation, screen reader support.
* **Themeable**: CSS variables and dark mode.
* **Composable**: Every component accepts `asChild`.
* **TypeScript-first**: Fully typed APIs, no `any`.

## Getting Started

### Install via CLI

```bash
npx @gentleduck/cli init
```

### Add a component

```bash
npx @gentleduck/cli add button
```

### Use it

```tsx
import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'

export default function App() {
  return <Button>Click me</Button>
}
```

## The Ecosystem

Duck UI is the styled layer on top of the gentleduck stack:

| Package | Role |
|---------|------|
| `duck-primitives` | Headless, accessible primitives |
| `duck-vim` | Keyboard command engine |
| `duck-calendar` | Headless calendar + date logic |
| `duck-variants` | `cva()` variant system |
| `duck-motion` | Animation tokens |
| `duck-cli` | Component scaffolding CLI |
| `duck-ui` | Styled components (this package) |

## 0.8.1

### Patch Changes

* 47f9fd3: `FieldDescription` is `text-xs` and, together with `FieldError`, tucks up against the label or control above it in a vertical `Field`. `FieldError` skips entries without a `message`: one message renders as plain text, several as a list, and none renders nothing, where an array of empty entries used to render an empty list.
* a6f949d: The `TooltipArrow`, `PopoverArrow`, `HoverCardArrow` and `DropdownMenuArrow` outline is 1px, like the content border it meets, and is drawn over the fill so the line sits on the curve instead of outside it. The fill comes from `--popover` directly, so the arrow no longer needs the `fill-popover` class.
* a592829: `Sidebar` and `MotionSidebar` sit at `z-5` instead of `z-10`. `SidebarInset` has `min-w-0`, so wide content such as a table scrolls inside it instead of pushing the page wider, and a hidden `SidebarGroupLabel` in icon mode no longer takes clicks. `Badge` size `sm` uses `.75rem` text. Chart tooltip and legend icons keep a `size-*` class you give them instead of being forced to the default size.

## 0.8.0

### Minor Changes

* 0c295e1: `CommandDialog` takes `title` and `description` for its screen-reader title and description, so they can be translated. They default to the English text it hard-coded before, `Command palette` and `Search for commands and navigation items`.
* 9075a3d: `PreviewPanel` and `MotionPreviewPanel` start locked: the wheel over a panel scrolls the page it sits in instead of zooming, and drag and pinch do nothing until the user presses the new lock button beside the zoom controls. The zoom buttons work either way. Pass `defaultLocked={false}` where the panel is the page's main content, and `lockText` and `unlockText` to translate the button. A new `actions` prop renders your own buttons in the toolbar before the zoom controls, and still renders with `showControls={false}`.

  `PreviewPanelDialog` puts its fullscreen button in that toolbar instead of over the bottom corner of the content, takes the same `defaultLocked`, `lockText` and `unlockText` for its inline panel, and opens the fullscreen panel unlocked.

  If a panel relied on the wheel zooming straight away, add `defaultLocked={false}`.

### Patch Changes

* 0f9c5b2: `Breadcrumb` keeps an `aria-label` you pass instead of overwriting it with `breadcrumb`, which stays the default. Its type drops the `separator` prop, which the component never read; if you passed one, remove it and pass `BreadcrumbSeparator` children as before.
* 4d66971: The `Button` and `MotionButton` loading spinner holds still when the user has asked for reduced motion (`motion-reduce:animate-none`).
* 678e0d2: `CommandList` caps the box that scrolls. The `max-h-75` limit and your `className` sat on the list inside the scroll area, so a long list spilled past the cap instead of scrolling; both now go on the viewport. The list also scrolls with the wheel and touch when it is portalled out of a modal, such as a combobox inside a dialog, where the modal's scroll lock used to swallow the gesture.
* 60d564c: `Input` is `h-9`, the height of the `Select` trigger, `Button` and `InputGroup` it sits beside in a form row or a button group; it was `h-8`. `Input`, `Textarea`, the `Select` and `MotionSelect` triggers and the default `Button` share one `shadow-xs`, where the select and button used `shadow-sm` and the input and textarea had none.

## 0.7.0

### Minor Changes

* 8d18fa6: Every component follows the direction set once with `DirectionProvider` or `<html dir>`. Physical sides (`left`/`right` on sheet, sidebar, toasts, and popups) mirror in RTL instead of staying put, arrows and chevrons flip where they point along the inline axis, and keyboard navigation in tabs, menubar, and calendar follows the visual order. Progress fills from the inline-start edge, charts keep their SVG labels anchored, carousel passes the direction to Embla, JSON stays LTR inside the JSON editor, and `Kbd` keeps key labels in typing order. Preview panel controls accept `zoomInText`, `zoomOutText`, and `resetText` for translated labels.
* 22e853d: Add `Typeset`, prose styles for rendered HTML and markdown such as docs pages, blog posts, and streamed AI replies. Wrap content in `<Typeset>` (or add the `typeset` class) and headings, lists, tables, code, and quotes get consistent sizes and spacing driven by three variables: `--typeset-size`, `--typeset-leading`, and `--typeset-flow`. Blocks only take a top margin, so streamed content never shifts what is already on screen. Opt a subtree out with `not-typeset`. The styles ship as `@gentleduck/registry-ui/typeset.css`.
* 27ffc5e: `TabsContent` takes `renderOnce`: the panel mounts the first time its tab opens and then stays mounted, hidden, so form input, scroll position, and fetched data survive tab switches. `forceMount` now keeps a panel mounted from the start, before its tab is ever opened. Kept panels get `display: none` and `aria-hidden`.

  By default an inactive panel now unmounts. Before, every panel stayed mounted after its first open no matter which props you passed. If you relied on that to keep state across tab switches, add `renderOnce`.

### Patch Changes

* 2f92193: Components share one motion language. Popups and dialogs set enter and exit durations with `animation-duration-*` (200ms in and 150ms out; 300ms and 200ms for dialogs and sheets) on the shared `--gentleduck-motion-ease`. Transitions name the properties they animate instead of `transition-all`, and the sidebar, accordion, and collapsible use the same easing. Motion popovers use `springBouncy`, alert dialogs `springStiff` for both overlay and content, and the motion sheet overlay `tweenSlow`.
* 33c4389: The `Command` shortcut docs use `mod+k`, which is Cmd on Mac and Ctrl elsewhere, instead of `ctrl+K`.
* ed5fb65: The navigation menu viewport measures its content before the first paint, so opening a menu no longer flashes an empty 0x0 box for a frame. The styled viewport also fades as it zooms in and out.
* c9fe51c: Tailwind classes use their v4 forms: `size-*` instead of matching `h-*`/`w-*` pairs, `outline-hidden` instead of `outline-none`, and `focus-visible:` rings on close buttons, so a mouse click no longer leaves a focus ring. Popover, tooltip, hover card, and dropdown menu set their border colour with a class instead of an inline style, and the slider thumb uses `bg-background` so it follows the theme.
* 8ed39e5: `ScrollArea` shows the native scrollbar again. The viewport hard-coded `scrollbar-none`, so content scrolled with no visible bar, and a `viewportClassName` could not bring it back. The bar now uses your global `::-webkit-scrollbar` styles; pass `viewportClassName="scrollbar-none"` to hide it.
* 1b0f91a: `SheetContent` renders its children before the close button, so the absolutely positioned button stays on top of full-bleed content and comes after it in tab order.
* Updated dependencies \[ed5fb65]
* Updated dependencies \[8d18fa6]
  * @gentleduck/primitives@0.5.0

## 0.6.2

### Patch Changes

* 65728a4: `MotionTableRow`, `MotionAlertTitle`, `MotionAlertDescription` and `MotionTypographyListItem` bring their own `LazyMotion`. They need no context from their motion root, so they can sit in the plain `Table`, `Alert` or list, where nothing loaded Motion's features and their entrance animation never ran.
* ee71f99: `toDirection` accepts only `ltr` and `rtl`. It checked `dir in DIRECTION_DICTIONARY`, which also matches keys inherited from `Object.prototype`, so `toDirection('toString')` returned `'toString'` as a direction.
* cafcba7: `unsafeHtml` takes priority over `children` whenever it is passed, as its docs say. `PreviewPanel`, `MotionPreviewPanel` and `PreviewPanelDialog` tested its truthiness, so `unsafeHtml=""` rendered `children` instead.

## 0.6.1

### Patch Changes

* bfa58d9: - Disabled and `aria-disabled` controls show a `cursor-not-allowed` cursor. They relied on `pointer-events-none` alone, which hid the cursor instead of showing that the control is disabled.
  * An icon inside a component can be resized with its own `size-*` class, without `!`. The components' default `[&_svg]:size-4` now steps aside when the icon carries a size.
  * The `Switch` thumb grows from the correct side in left-to-right layouts. Its transform origins were the right-to-left ones; they now follow the direction.
  * `PopoverArrow`'s props no longer reference the primitive's internal `Scope` type, which made declaration emit non-portable.
* Updated dependencies \[1681854]
* Updated dependencies \[bfa58d9]
  * @gentleduck/calendar@0.5.0
  * @gentleduck/primitives@0.4.0

## 0.6.0

### Minor Changes

* a157bae: Add styled arrow components for overlay components: `TooltipArrow`, `PopoverArrow`, `HoverCardArrow`, and `DropdownMenuArrow`. Arrows use a bezier curve SVG shape that seamlessly joins the content border, with border stroke on curved sides only via a two-path technique. Border color is customizable via `--tooltip-border-color`, `--popover-border-color`, `--hover-card-border-color`, and `--dropdown-menu-border-color` CSS custom properties on the respective content elements. Also fixes `overflow-hidden` removal from content containers so arrows are not clipped, adds `relative` positioning for correct arrow animation, and restructures `DropdownMenuContent` with an inner scrollable wrapper to decouple overflow from the arrow's containing block.

## 0.5.0

### Minor Changes

* 95638de: Audit-driven refactor across all 15 public packages. Closes type holes, hardens security boundaries, eliminates dead code, and dedups duplicated patterns.

  **Highlights**

  * `duck-docs` — CompiledMdxBody branded type gates `new Function(body)`; sanitizeSvg covers SMIL, unquoted javascript: URIs, nested script, CSS url(), bare iframe; code-preview tag + attr allowlists
  * `duck-registry-build` — safe-path containment at every fs sink; per-phase Zod cache schemas; JSON.stringify in generated TSX; cache manifest rejection on tamper
  * `duck-cli` — install pipeline path containment unified across add/init/update; env-var allowlist contract reconciled with one-time warning; aliases.ui regex validation
  * `duck-primitives` — `observe-element-rect` rAF loop guard (no leak when empty); `compose-ref` useCallback memo fix; popper forwardRef restored for R18 peer compat
  * `duck-hooks` — `useDebounce` is now a real hook (stable identity, unmount cleanup); `useStableId` delegates to React.useId (SSR-safe); `scheduleTransitionTimeout` rename strips two `useHookAtTopLevel` lint suppressions
  * `duck-lazy` — spread order fix restores the lazy swap; `next/image` moved behind `/lazy-image-next` subpath so non-Next consumers don't pull the peer
  * `duck-vim` — single document listener fans out to chord matcher + sequence manager; canonical modifier order; `requireReset` auto-clears for chord bindings; all three hook dep arrays corrected
  * `duck-variants` — `Props<T, D>` makes defaulted variant keys optional and non-defaulted required; bounded `preludeCache` LRU; second-layer `filter2` set eliminates last clone in hot path
  * `duck-ttest` — `predictates/` renamed to `predicates/`, twin dirs deleted, type-utility duplicates reconciled to canonical sources, `IsVoid` actually distinguishes void from undefined now
  * `duck-calendar` — `./*` wildcard export removed; falsy-zero `weekStartDay: 0` (Sunday) bug fixed; Gregorian helpers extracted; Hebrew `addMonths` uses Metonic cycle
  * `duck-libs` — `cnMemo` bounded LRU; `filteredObject` rejects typo keys at compile time; `parseDate` rejects ambiguous one-token inputs
  * `duck-query` — single AnyReq boundary cast replaces 14 `as any`; param regex escape; throws on unresolved `:tokens`
  * `registers` — schema tightened (`z.any()` removed); ~1000 LoC of identical block-registry boilerplate replaced with builders
  * `registry-ui` — `_audio` / `_upload` (~1.1K LoC) deleted; `motion-shell` HOC + `withMotion` collapses simple motion clones; `toDirection()` narrower replaces 52 `as IDirection.Kind` casts; chart `CSS_NAMED_COLORS` finite allowlist
  * `duck-motion` — refcounted body `pointer-events` ownership; easing/blur/duration token dedup; half of public exports were unused and removed

  Tests: 3133+ across the monorepo, all green. Type-checks clean across every project. No commits skipped hooks.

## 0.8.1

### Patch Changes

* 47f9fd3: `FieldDescription` is `text-xs` and, together with `FieldError`, tucks up against the label or control above it in a vertical `Field`. `FieldError` skips entries without a `message`: one message renders as plain text, several as a list, and none renders nothing, where an array of empty entries used to render an empty list.
* a6f949d: The `TooltipArrow`, `PopoverArrow`, `HoverCardArrow` and `DropdownMenuArrow` outline is 1px, like the content border it meets, and is drawn over the fill so the line sits on the curve instead of outside it. The fill comes from `--popover` directly, so the arrow no longer needs the `fill-popover` class.
* a592829: `Sidebar` and `MotionSidebar` sit at `z-5` instead of `z-10`. `SidebarInset` has `min-w-0`, so wide content such as a table scrolls inside it instead of pushing the page wider, and a hidden `SidebarGroupLabel` in icon mode no longer takes clicks. `Badge` size `sm` uses `.75rem` text. Chart tooltip and legend icons keep a `size-*` class you give them instead of being forced to the default size.

## 0.8.0

### Minor Changes

* 0c295e1: `CommandDialog` takes `title` and `description` for its screen-reader title and description, so they can be translated. They default to the English text it hard-coded before, `Command palette` and `Search for commands and navigation items`.
* 9075a3d: `PreviewPanel` and `MotionPreviewPanel` start locked: the wheel over a panel scrolls the page it sits in instead of zooming, and drag and pinch do nothing until the user presses the new lock button beside the zoom controls. The zoom buttons work either way. Pass `defaultLocked={false}` where the panel is the page's main content, and `lockText` and `unlockText` to translate the button. A new `actions` prop renders your own buttons in the toolbar before the zoom controls, and still renders with `showControls={false}`.

  `PreviewPanelDialog` puts its fullscreen button in that toolbar instead of over the bottom corner of the content, takes the same `defaultLocked`, `lockText` and `unlockText` for its inline panel, and opens the fullscreen panel unlocked.

  If a panel relied on the wheel zooming straight away, add `defaultLocked={false}`.

### Patch Changes

* 0f9c5b2: `Breadcrumb` keeps an `aria-label` you pass instead of overwriting it with `breadcrumb`, which stays the default. Its type drops the `separator` prop, which the component never read; if you passed one, remove it and pass `BreadcrumbSeparator` children as before.
* 4d66971: The `Button` and `MotionButton` loading spinner holds still when the user has asked for reduced motion (`motion-reduce:animate-none`).
* 678e0d2: `CommandList` caps the box that scrolls. The `max-h-75` limit and your `className` sat on the list inside the scroll area, so a long list spilled past the cap instead of scrolling; both now go on the viewport. The list also scrolls with the wheel and touch when it is portalled out of a modal, such as a combobox inside a dialog, where the modal's scroll lock used to swallow the gesture.
* 60d564c: `Input` is `h-9`, the height of the `Select` trigger, `Button` and `InputGroup` it sits beside in a form row or a button group; it was `h-8`. `Input`, `Textarea`, the `Select` and `MotionSelect` triggers and the default `Button` share one `shadow-xs`, where the select and button used `shadow-sm` and the input and textarea had none.

## 0.7.0

### Minor Changes

* 8d18fa6: Every component follows the direction set once with `DirectionProvider` or `<html dir>`. Physical sides (`left`/`right` on sheet, sidebar, toasts, and popups) mirror in RTL instead of staying put, arrows and chevrons flip where they point along the inline axis, and keyboard navigation in tabs, menubar, and calendar follows the visual order. Progress fills from the inline-start edge, charts keep their SVG labels anchored, carousel passes the direction to Embla, JSON stays LTR inside the JSON editor, and `Kbd` keeps key labels in typing order. Preview panel controls accept `zoomInText`, `zoomOutText`, and `resetText` for translated labels.
* 22e853d: Add `Typeset`, prose styles for rendered HTML and markdown such as docs pages, blog posts, and streamed AI replies. Wrap content in `<Typeset>` (or add the `typeset` class) and headings, lists, tables, code, and quotes get consistent sizes and spacing driven by three variables: `--typeset-size`, `--typeset-leading`, and `--typeset-flow`. Blocks only take a top margin, so streamed content never shifts what is already on screen. Opt a subtree out with `not-typeset`. The styles ship as `@gentleduck/registry-ui/typeset.css`.
* 27ffc5e: `TabsContent` takes `renderOnce`: the panel mounts the first time its tab opens and then stays mounted, hidden, so form input, scroll position, and fetched data survive tab switches. `forceMount` now keeps a panel mounted from the start, before its tab is ever opened. Kept panels get `display: none` and `aria-hidden`.

  By default an inactive panel now unmounts. Before, every panel stayed mounted after its first open no matter which props you passed. If you relied on that to keep state across tab switches, add `renderOnce`.

### Patch Changes

* 2f92193: Components share one motion language. Popups and dialogs set enter and exit durations with `animation-duration-*` (200ms in and 150ms out; 300ms and 200ms for dialogs and sheets) on the shared `--gentleduck-motion-ease`. Transitions name the properties they animate instead of `transition-all`, and the sidebar, accordion, and collapsible use the same easing. Motion popovers use `springBouncy`, alert dialogs `springStiff` for both overlay and content, and the motion sheet overlay `tweenSlow`.
* 33c4389: The `Command` shortcut docs use `mod+k`, which is Cmd on Mac and Ctrl elsewhere, instead of `ctrl+K`.
* ed5fb65: The navigation menu viewport measures its content before the first paint, so opening a menu no longer flashes an empty 0x0 box for a frame. The styled viewport also fades as it zooms in and out.
* c9fe51c: Tailwind classes use their v4 forms: `size-*` instead of matching `h-*`/`w-*` pairs, `outline-hidden` instead of `outline-none`, and `focus-visible:` rings on close buttons, so a mouse click no longer leaves a focus ring. Popover, tooltip, hover card, and dropdown menu set their border colour with a class instead of an inline style, and the slider thumb uses `bg-background` so it follows the theme.
* 8ed39e5: `ScrollArea` shows the native scrollbar again. The viewport hard-coded `scrollbar-none`, so content scrolled with no visible bar, and a `viewportClassName` could not bring it back. The bar now uses your global `::-webkit-scrollbar` styles; pass `viewportClassName="scrollbar-none"` to hide it.
* 1b0f91a: `SheetContent` renders its children before the close button, so the absolutely positioned button stays on top of full-bleed content and comes after it in tab order.
* Updated dependencies \[ed5fb65]
* Updated dependencies \[8d18fa6]
  * @gentleduck/primitives@0.5.0

## 0.6.2

### Patch Changes

* 65728a4: `MotionTableRow`, `MotionAlertTitle`, `MotionAlertDescription` and `MotionTypographyListItem` bring their own `LazyMotion`. They need no context from their motion root, so they can sit in the plain `Table`, `Alert` or list, where nothing loaded Motion's features and their entrance animation never ran.
* ee71f99: `toDirection` accepts only `ltr` and `rtl`. It checked `dir in DIRECTION_DICTIONARY`, which also matches keys inherited from `Object.prototype`, so `toDirection('toString')` returned `'toString'` as a direction.
* cafcba7: `unsafeHtml` takes priority over `children` whenever it is passed, as its docs say. `PreviewPanel`, `MotionPreviewPanel` and `PreviewPanelDialog` tested its truthiness, so `unsafeHtml=""` rendered `children` instead.

## 0.6.1

### Patch Changes

* bfa58d9: - Disabled and `aria-disabled` controls show a `cursor-not-allowed` cursor. They relied on `pointer-events-none` alone, which hid the cursor instead of showing that the control is disabled.
  * An icon inside a component can be resized with its own `size-*` class, without `!`. The components' default `[&_svg]:size-4` now steps aside when the icon carries a size.
  * The `Switch` thumb grows from the correct side in left-to-right layouts. Its transform origins were the right-to-left ones; they now follow the direction.
  * `PopoverArrow`'s props no longer reference the primitive's internal `Scope` type, which made declaration emit non-portable.

## 0.6.0

### Minor Changes

* a157bae: Add styled arrow components for overlay components: `TooltipArrow`, `PopoverArrow`, `HoverCardArrow`, and `DropdownMenuArrow`. Arrows use a bezier curve SVG shape that seamlessly joins the content border, with border stroke on curved sides only via a two-path technique. Border color is customizable via `--tooltip-border-color`, `--popover-border-color`, `--hover-card-border-color`, and `--dropdown-menu-border-color` CSS custom properties on the respective content elements. Also fixes `overflow-hidden` removal from content containers so arrows are not clipped, adds `relative` positioning for correct arrow animation, and restructures `DropdownMenuContent` with an inner scrollable wrapper to decouple overflow from the arrow's containing block.

## 0.5.0

### Minor Changes

* 95638de: Audit-driven refactor across all 15 public packages. Closes type holes, hardens security boundaries, eliminates dead code, and dedups duplicated patterns.

  **Highlights**

  * `duck-docs` — CompiledMdxBody branded type gates `new Function(body)`; sanitizeSvg covers SMIL, unquoted javascript: URIs, nested script, CSS url(), bare iframe; code-preview tag + attr allowlists
  * `duck-registry-build` — safe-path containment at every fs sink; per-phase Zod cache schemas; JSON.stringify in generated TSX; cache manifest rejection on tamper
  * `duck-cli` — install pipeline path containment unified across add/init/update; env-var allowlist contract reconciled with one-time warning; aliases.ui regex validation
  * `duck-primitives` — `observe-element-rect` rAF loop guard (no leak when empty); `compose-ref` useCallback memo fix; popper forwardRef restored for R18 peer compat
  * `duck-hooks` — `useDebounce` is now a real hook (stable identity, unmount cleanup); `useStableId` delegates to React.useId (SSR-safe); `scheduleTransitionTimeout` rename strips two `useHookAtTopLevel` lint suppressions
  * `duck-lazy` — spread order fix restores the lazy swap; `next/image` moved behind `/lazy-image-next` subpath so non-Next consumers don't pull the peer
  * `duck-vim` — single document listener fans out to chord matcher + sequence manager; canonical modifier order; `requireReset` auto-clears for chord bindings; all three hook dep arrays corrected
  * `duck-variants` — `Props<T, D>` makes defaulted variant keys optional and non-defaulted required; bounded `preludeCache` LRU; second-layer `filter2` set eliminates last clone in hot path
  * `duck-ttest` — `predictates/` renamed to `predicates/`, twin dirs deleted, type-utility duplicates reconciled to canonical sources, `IsVoid` actually distinguishes void from undefined now
  * `duck-calendar` — `./*` wildcard export removed; falsy-zero `weekStartDay: 0` (Sunday) bug fixed; Gregorian helpers extracted; Hebrew `addMonths` uses Metonic cycle
  * `duck-libs` — `cnMemo` bounded LRU; `filteredObject` rejects typo keys at compile time; `parseDate` rejects ambiguous one-token inputs
  * `duck-query` — single AnyReq boundary cast replaces 14 `as any`; param regex escape; throws on unresolved `:tokens`
  * `registers` — schema tightened (`z.any()` removed); ~1000 LoC of identical block-registry boilerplate replaced with builders
  * `registry-ui` — `_audio` / `_upload` (~1.1K LoC) deleted; `motion-shell` HOC + `withMotion` collapses simple motion clones; `toDirection()` narrower replaces 52 `as IDirection.Kind` casts; chart `CSS_NAMED_COLORS` finite allowlist
  * `duck-motion` — refcounted body `pointer-events` ownership; easing/blur/duration token dedup; half of public exports were unused and removed

  Tests: 3133+ across the monorepo, all green. Type-checks clean across every project. No commits skipped hooks.

You can use `@gentleduck/ui` from JavaScript projects.

The source and docs are authored in TypeScript, but runtime usage works the same in JavaScript. You can copy component code and remove type annotations where needed.

## Notes for JavaScript users

* Install and use components exactly as shown in the docs.
* Ignore type-only imports and type annotations in TypeScript snippets.
* Keep your project aliases configured (`@/*` etc.) so copied component imports resolve correctly.

<Callout icon={<Lightbulb />}>
  TypeScript is recommended for better editor support and safer refactors, but it is not required to use the components.
</Callout>

## Next steps

* [Installation](/duck-ui/installation)  -  Set up your project
* [CLI](/duck-cli)  -  Add components quickly
* [Components](/duck-ui)  -  Browse available UI components

They work well with the other components and are fully customizable to fit your project. [Browse the Charts Library](/charts). ## Philosophy Charts turn data into stories. We wrap Recharts because building accessible, responsive, animated SVG charts from scratch is a multi-month project - not a component library feature. We build on Floating UI because positioning against viewport edges, scroll containers, and dynamic layouts is harder than it looks. The `data-state` and `data-side` attributes give you animation hooks without JavaScript state management. * **Floating UI powered positioning** - Smart placement with `flip`, `shift`, and `offset` middleware. * **State-aware styling hooks** - `data-state` and `data-side` attributes for state and placement styling. * **Transform-origin variable** - Uses `--gentleduck-tooltip-content-transform-origin` for direction-aware animations. * **Customizable delays** - Configure open and close delays globally with `TooltipProvider` or per tooltip with `delayDuration` and `closeDelay`. * **Flexible triggers** - Wrap any element using `asChild`. * **Accessible by default** - Implements proper ARIA attributes and keyboard navigation. * **Portal rendering** - Renders tooltips in a portal to avoid layout clipping. ## Left and right mirror in RTL | | `theme` | `'light' \| 'dark' \| 'system'` | `'system'` | Toast theme. Auto-detected from `next-themes` `useTheme()` | | `style` | `React.CSSProperties` | - | Merged over the popover colours the toasts take, `--normal-bg`, `--normal-border` and `--normal-text`, so one of those can be overridden and the rest kept | | `...props` | `ToasterProps` | - | Additional props inherited from the `sonner` toaster. | ### SonnerUpload | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `progress` | `number` | (required) | Current upload progress percentage (0--100) | | `attachments` | `number` | (required) | Number of files being uploaded | | `remainingTime` | `number` | - | Estimated remaining upload time in seconds | | `onCancel` | `(e: React.MouseEvent, dismiss: (id: string) => void) => void` | - | Callback triggered when the Cancel button is clicked. Receives the click event and a function to dismiss the toast by ID | | `onComplete` | `(e: React.MouseEvent, dismiss: (id: string) => void) => void` | - | Callback triggered when the Complete button is clicked. Receives the click event and a function to dismiss the toast by ID | While `progress` is under 100, `SonnerUpload` shows a spinning `Loader`, the time left when `remainingTime` is above zero, and a Cancel button. From 100 up it shows a `CircleCheck`, a full bar at 100%, reads "Upload complete", says it is safe to close the browser, and offers Complete. The bar is named "Upload progress". It adds no live region of its own, since the `Toaster` already announces what changes in a toast. ### Utility Function #### `formatTime(seconds: number): string` Formats a duration in seconds into a human-readable string: * Returns days if >= 1 day (`'Xd'`), * else hours if >= 1 hour (`'Xh'`), * else minutes if >= 1 minute (`'Xm'`), * else seconds (`'Xs'`). If you find a broken composition, please [file an issue](https://github.com/gentleeduck/gentleduck/issues). Use `MotionEmpty`, `MotionEmptyMedia`, `MotionEmptyTitle`, `MotionEmptyDescription`, and `MotionEmptyContent` for staggered entrance animations powered by [motion](https://motion.dev). Every element shares the same `scaleIn` entrance (fade, scale, and blur) with a bouncy spring transition, staggered by increasing delays. ```tsx 'use client' import { MotionButton } from '~/components/button' import { EmptyHeader, MotionEmpty, MotionEmptyContent, MotionEmptyDescription, MotionEmptyMedia, MotionEmptyTitle, } from '~/components/empty' import { IconInbox } from '@tabler/icons-react' export function Demo() { return ( Your Inbox is Empty No messages waiting for you. Wraps the `EmptyHeader` and `EmptyContent` components. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `dir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl'` | - | Text direction override. Resolved via `useDirection` (`dir` prop -> `DirectionProvider` -> ``). | | `className` | `string` | `--` | Additional CSS classes | | `children` | `React.ReactNode` | `--` | Empty state content | | `...props` | `React.ComponentProps<'div'>` | - | Additional props to spread to the div | ### EmptyHeader The `EmptyHeader` component wraps the empty media, title, and description. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `className` | `string` | `--` | Additional CSS classes | | `children` | `React.ReactNode` | `--` | Header content (media, title, description) | | `...props` | `React.ComponentProps<'div'>` | - | Additional props to spread to the div | ### EmptyMedia Use the `EmptyMedia` component to display the media of the empty state such as an icon or an image. You can also use it to display other components such as an avatar. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `variant` | `'default' \| 'icon'` | `'default'` | Visual variant of the media container | | `className` | `string` | `--` | Additional CSS classes | | `children` | `React.ReactNode` | `--` | Media content (icon, avatar, image) | | `...props` | `React.ComponentProps<'div'>` | - | Additional props to spread to the div | ### EmptyTitle Use the `EmptyTitle` component to display the title of the empty state. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `className` | `string` | `--` | Additional CSS classes | | `children` | `React.ReactNode` | `--` | Title text | | `...props` | `React.ComponentProps<'div'>` | - | Additional props to spread to the div | ### EmptyDescription Use the `EmptyDescription` component to display the description of the empty state. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `className` | `string` | `--` | Additional CSS classes | | `children` | `React.ReactNode` | `--` | Description text | | `...props` | `React.ComponentProps<'p'>` | - | Additional props to spread to the description element (renders as a `div`) | ### EmptyContent Use the `EmptyContent` component to display the content of the empty state such as a button, input or a link. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `className` | `string` | `--` | Additional CSS classes | | `children` | `React.ReactNode` | `--` | Action content (buttons, links, inputs) | | `...props` | `React.ComponentProps<'div'>` | - | Additional props to spread to the div | ### MotionEmpty Same props as `Empty`. Adds a `scaleIn` entrance animation (fade, scale, and blur) with a bouncy spring transition. Requires the `motion` package. ### MotionEmptyMedia Same props as `EmptyMedia`. Adds a `scaleIn` entrance (fade, scale, and blur) with a bouncy spring transition and a 50ms delay. Requires the `motion` package. ### MotionEmptyTitle Same props as `EmptyTitle`. Adds a `scaleIn` entrance (fade, scale, and blur) with a bouncy spring transition and a 100ms delay. Requires the `motion` package. ### MotionEmptyDescription Same props as `EmptyDescription`. Adds a `scaleIn` entrance (fade, scale, and blur) with a bouncy spring transition and a 150ms delay. Requires the `motion` package. ### MotionEmptyContent Same props as `EmptyContent`. Adds a `scaleIn` entrance (fade, scale, and blur) with a bouncy spring transition and a 200ms delay. Requires the `motion` package.

The Joke Tax Chronicles Once upon a time, in a far-off land, there was a very lazy king who spent all day lounging on his throne. One day, his advisors came to him with a problem: the kingdom was running out of money. The King's Plan The king thought long and hard, and finally came up with{' '} a brilliant plan : he would tax the jokes in the kingdom. "After all," he said, "everyone enjoys a good joke, so it's only fair that they should pay for the privilege." The Joke Tax The king's subjects were not amused. They grumbled and complained, but the king was firm:
  • 1st level of puns: 5 gold coins
  • 2nd level of jokes: 10 gold coins
  • 3rd level of one-liners : 20 gold coins
    •  As a result, people stopped telling jokes, and the kingdom fell into a gloom. But there was one person who refused to let the king's foolishness get him down: a court jester named Jokester. Jokester's Revolt Jokester began sneaking into the castle in the middle of the night and leaving jokes all over the place: under the king's pillow, in his soup, even in the royal toilet. The king was furious, but he couldn't seem to stop Jokester. And then, one day, the people of the kingdom discovered that the jokes left by Jokester were so funny that they couldn't help but laugh. All other sub-components stay the same. ## API Reference ### NavigationMenu Root container that wraps the navigation menu and optionally renders the viewport. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `value` | `string` | - | Controlled value of the active menu item | | `defaultValue` | `string` | - | Default active value for uncontrolled usage | | `onValueChange` | `(value: string) => void` | - | Callback when the active value changes | | `viewport` | `boolean` | `true` | Whether to render the `NavigationMenuViewport` automatically | | `dir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl'` | - | Text direction. Resolved by primitives `useDirection` (`dir` prop -> `DirectionProvider` -> ``) and inherited by descendants. | | `orientation` | `'horizontal' \| 'vertical'` | `'horizontal'` | The orientation of the menu | | `delayDuration` | `number` | `200` | Duration in ms from when the pointer enters a trigger until the content opens. A click on the trigger before then cancels the open | | `skipDelayDuration` | `number` | `300` | Duration in ms a user has to enter another trigger without incurring a delay again | | `closeDelay` | `number` | `150` | Duration in ms an item stays open after the pointer leaves it | | `activationMode` | `'automatic' \| 'manual'` | `'automatic'` | `manual` opens and closes an item only on a click of its trigger, and ignores the pointer resting on it | | `className` | `string` | - | Additional CSS classes for the root element | | `children` | `React.ReactNode` | - | Navigation menu list and other elements | | `...props` | `React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef` | - | Additional props inherited from `NavigationMenu.Root`. | ### NavigationMenuList | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `className` | `string` | `--` | Additional CSS classes for the list element | | `...props` | `React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef` | - | Additional props inherited from `NavigationMenu.List`. | ### NavigationMenuItem | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `className` | `string` | `--` | Additional CSS classes for the menu item | | `...props` | `React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef` | - | Additional props inherited from `NavigationMenu.Item`. | ### NavigationMenuTrigger | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `className` | `string` | `--` | Additional CSS classes for the trigger | | `children` | `React.ReactNode` | `--` | Trigger label content. A chevron icon is appended automatically | | `...props` | `React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef` | - | Additional props inherited from `NavigationMenu.Trigger`. | ### NavigationMenuContent | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `className` | `string` | `--` | Additional CSS classes for the content panel | | `...props` | `React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef` | - | Additional props inherited from `NavigationMenu.Content`. | ### NavigationMenuLink | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `className` | `string` | `--` | Additional CSS classes for the link | | `active` | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the link as the current page and draws it highlighted | | `closeOnSelect` | `boolean` | `true` | `false` keeps the menu open once the link is selected. A click with Cmd, Ctrl, Shift or Alt held leaves it open either way, since the link opens elsewhere and the page stays | | `onSelect` | `(event: Event) => void` | - | Called when the link is chosen. `event.preventDefault()` keeps the menu open | | `...props` | `React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef` | - | Additional props inherited from `NavigationMenu.Link`. | ### NavigationMenuViewport | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `className` | `string` | `--` | Additional CSS classes for the viewport | | `...props` | `React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef` | - | Additional props inherited from `NavigationMenu.Viewport`. | ### NavigationMenuIndicator Place it in `NavigationMenuList`. It draws an arrow under the open trigger, or beside it in a vertical menu. | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `className` | `string` | `--` | Additional CSS classes for the indicator | | `forceMount` | `true` | - | Keeps the indicator drawn, as `data-state="hidden"`, while no item is open | | `...props` | `React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef` | - | Additional props inherited from `NavigationMenu.Indicator`. | ### navigationMenuTriggerStyle A `cva` variant function that returns the default trigger styling classes. Use it to style non-trigger elements (e.g. plain links) to match the trigger appearance. ```tsx import { navigationMenuTriggerStyle } from "@/components/ui/navigation-menu" Documentation ``` ### MotionNavigationMenu Same props as `NavigationMenu`. Its viewport opens with a `scaleIn` animation (fade, scale, and blur) on a bouncy spring and stays mounted through its exit, in place of the CSS animation `NavigationMenuViewport` plays. With `viewport={false}` the contents keep their CSS animation. Requires the `motion` package.

const MotionPagination = React.forwardRef<
  React.ComponentRef<typeof PaginationPrimitive.Root>,
  React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof PaginationPrimitive.Root>
>(({ className, ...props }, ref) => {
  const content = useMotionPreset(scaleIn, { transition: springBouncy })
  return (
    <LazyMotion features={loadDomAnimation}>
      <m.div initial={content.initial} animate={content.animate} transition={content.transition}>
        <PaginationPrimitive.Root
          className={cn('mx-auto flex w-full justify-center', className)}
          ref={ref}
          {...props}
        />
      </m.div>
    </LazyMotion>
  )
})

        data-slot="pagination-link"
        ref={ref}
        initial={content.initial}
        animate={content.animate}
        transition={content.transition}
        whileTap={tapScale}
        {...(props as Omit<
          React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'a'>,

      />
    </LazyMotion>
  )
})

  ({ className, isActive, size = 'icon', ...props }, ref) => (
    <a
      aria-current={isActive ? 'page' : undefined}
      className={cn(
        buttonVariants({
          size,
          variant: isActive ? 'outline' : 'ghost',
        }),
        className,
      )}
      data-slot="pagination-link"
      ref={ref}
      {...props}
    />
  ),
)
PaginationLink.displayName = 'PaginationLink'

const PaginationPrevious = React.forwardRef<
  HTMLAnchorElement,
  React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof PaginationLink> & { text?: string }
>(({ className, text = 'Previous', ...props }, ref) => (
  <PaginationLink
    aria-label="Go to previous page"
    className={cn('gap-1 ps-2.5', className)}
    data-slot="pagination-previous"
    ref={ref}
    {...props}
    size="default">
    <ChevronLeft aria-hidden="true" className="size-4 rtl:rotate-180" />
    <span className="hidden sm:block">{text}</span>
  </PaginationLink>

PaginationPrevious.displayName = 'PaginationPrevious'

const PaginationNext = React.forwardRef<
  HTMLAnchorElement,
  React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof PaginationLink> & { text?: string }
>(({ className, text = 'Next', ...props }, ref) => (
  <PaginationLink
    aria-label="Go to next page"
    className={cn('gap-1 pe-2.5', className)}
    data-slot="pagination-next"
    ref={ref}
    {...props}
    size="default">
    <span className="hidden sm:block">{text}</span>
    <ChevronRight aria-hidden="true" className="size-4 rtl:rotate-180" />
  </PaginationLink>
))
PaginationNext.displayName = 'PaginationNext'

const PaginationEllipsis = React.forwardRef<
  HTMLSpanElement,
  React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<'span'> & { text?: string }
>(({ className, text = 'More pages', ...props }, ref) => (
  <span
    role="img"
    aria-label={text}
    className={cn('flex size-9 items-center justify-center', className)}
    data-slot="pagination-ellipsis"
    ref={ref}
    {...props}>

  </span>
))
PaginationEllipsis.displayName = 'PaginationEllipsis'

const PaginationPage = React.forwardRef<
  React.ComponentRef<typeof PaginationPrimitive.Page>,
  React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof PaginationPrimitive.Page>
>(({ className, ...props }, ref) => (
  <PaginationPrimitive.Page
    className={cn(
      buttonVariants({ size: 'icon', variant: 'ghost' }),
      'data-selected:border data-selected:border-input data-selected:bg-background data-selected:shadow-xs',
      className,
    )}
    ref={ref}
    {...props}
  />
))
PaginationPage.displayName = 'PaginationPage'

const renderPages = (items: IPagination.IRangeItem[]) =>
  items.map((item) => (
    <PaginationItem key={item}>
      {typeof item === 'number' ? <PaginationPage value={item} /> : <PaginationEllipsis />}
    </PaginationItem>
  ))

/** The root's pages, each in an item, with the ellipsis the same size as a page so the controls never shift. */
const PaginationPages = ({ children = renderPages }: IPagination.IPagesProps) => (
  <PaginationPrimitive.Pages>{children}</PaginationPrimitive.Pages>
)

function createTrigger(Trigger: typeof PaginationPrimitive.Next, Icon: LucideIcon, displayName: string) {
  const PaginationTrigger = React.forwardRef<
    React.ComponentRef<typeof Trigger>,
    React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<typeof Trigger>
  >(({ className, children, ...props }, ref) => (
    <Trigger className={cn(buttonVariants({ size: 'icon', variant: 'ghost' }), className)} ref={ref} {...props}>
      {children ?? <Icon aria-hidden="true" className="rtl:rotate-180" />}
    </Trigger>
  ))
  PaginationTrigger.displayName = displayName
  return PaginationTrigger
}

const PaginationFirstTrigger = createTrigger(PaginationPrimitive.First, ChevronsLeftIcon, 'PaginationFirstTrigger')
const PaginationPreviousTrigger = createTrigger(
  PaginationPrimitive.Previous,
  ChevronLeftIcon,
  'PaginationPreviousTrigger',
)
const PaginationNextTrigger = createTrigger(PaginationPrimitive.Next, ChevronRightIcon, 'PaginationNextTrigger')
const PaginationLastTrigger = createTrigger(PaginationPrimitive.Last, ChevronsRightIcon, 'PaginationLastTrigger')

const PaginationWrapper = (props: IDuckPaginationProps) => {
  const { className: wrapperClassName, dir, ...wrapperProps } = props.wrapper ?? {}
  const { className: contentClassName, ...contentProps } = props.content ?? {}
  const { className: itemClassName, ...itemProps } = props.item ?? {}
  const { className: rightClassName, icon: rightIcon, ...rightProps } = props.right ?? {}
  const { className: maxRightClassName, icon: maxRightIcon, ...maxRightProps } = props.maxRight ?? {}
  const { className: leftClassName, icon: leftIcon, ...leftProps } = props.left ?? {}
  const { className: maxLeftClassName, icon: maxLeftIcon, ...maxLeftProps } = props.maxLeft ?? {}
  const direction = useDirection(toDirection(dir))
  const StartIcon = direction === 'rtl' ? ChevronRightIcon : ChevronLeftIcon
  const EndIcon = direction === 'rtl' ? ChevronLeftIcon : ChevronRightIcon
  const StartDoubleIcon = direction === 'rtl' ? ChevronsRightIcon : ChevronsLeftIcon
  const EndDoubleIcon = direction === 'rtl' ? ChevronsLeftIcon : ChevronsRightIcon

  return (
    <Pagination className={cn('justify-end', wrapperClassName)} dir={direction} {...wrapperProps}>
      <PaginationContent className={cn('gap-2', contentClassName)} {...contentProps}>
        <PaginationItem className={cn(itemClassName)} {...itemProps}>
          <Button
            aria-label="Go to first page"
            className={cn('w-[32px] p-0', maxLeftClassName)}
            icon={maxLeftIcon === undefined ? <StartDoubleIcon aria-hidden="true" /> : maxLeftIcon}
            size="sm"
            variant="outline"
            {...maxLeftProps}
          />
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem className={cn(itemClassName)} {...itemProps}>
          <Button
            aria-label="Go to previous page"
            className={cn('w-[32px] p-0', leftClassName)}
            icon={leftIcon === undefined ? <StartIcon aria-hidden="true" /> : leftIcon}
            size="sm"
            variant="outline"
            {...leftProps}
          />
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem className={cn(itemClassName)} {...itemProps}>
          <Button
            aria-label="Go to next page"
            className={cn('w-[32px] p-0', rightClassName)}
            icon={rightIcon === undefined ? <EndIcon aria-hidden="true" /> : rightIcon}
            size="sm"
            variant="outline"
            {...rightProps}
          />
        </PaginationItem>
        <PaginationItem className={cn(itemClassName)} {...itemProps}>
          <Button
            aria-label="Go to last page"
            className={cn('w-[32px] p-0', maxRightClassName)}
            icon={maxRightIcon === undefined ? <EndDoubleIcon aria-hidden="true" /> : maxRightIcon}
            size="sm"
            variant="outline"
            {...maxRightProps}
          />
        </PaginationItem>
      </PaginationContent>
    </Pagination>
  )
}

  PaginationPage,
  PaginationPages,
  PaginationPrevious,
  PaginationPreviousTrigger,
  PaginationWrapper,
}

export function Demo() {

      </PaginationContent>
    </Pagination>
  )

import { PaginationWrapper } from '~/components/pagination'
import * as React from 'react'

const pageCount = 8

export function Demo() {
  const [page, setPage] = React.useState(1)
  const first = page === 1
  const last = page === pageCount

  return (
    <div className="flex items-center gap-4">
      <p className="text-muted-foreground text-sm">
        Page {page} of {pageCount}
      </p>
      <PaginationWrapper

        right={{ disabled: last, onClick: () => setPage(page + 1) }}
        wrapper={{ 'aria-label': 'Invoices' }}
      />
    </div>
  )
}

We provide the visual components (page buttons, next/previous, ellipsis) and let you wire them to your data layer. This separation means the same pagination UI works whether you're paginating a client-side array, an API, or a database cursor. Under the hood, this component composes `@gentleduck/primitives/pagination` for semantic structure and direction-aware behavior. Give the root a `pageCount` and it can also track the page for you: `PaginationPages` draws the pages around the current one, and the trigger parts move between them and disable themselves at either end. Every page draws the same number of items, so the triggers never move under the pointer. ## How It's Built B[PaginationContent] B --> C[PaginationItem] C --> D[PaginationPrevious] C --> E[PaginationLink] C --> F[PaginationNext] C --> G[PaginationEllipsis] B --> I[PaginationPages] I --> C C --> J[PaginationPage] C --> K[PaginationFirstTrigger / PreviousTrigger / NextTrigger / LastTrigger] A -.-> H[PaginationWrapper] `} /> ## Installation CLI Manual ```bash npx @gentleduck/cli add pagination ``` Install the following dependencies: ```bash npm install @gentleduck/libs @gentleduck/primitives ``` Add the `Button` component to your project. The `Pagination` component uses the [`Button`](/duck-ui/components/button) component. Make sure you have it installed in your project. import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogAction,
  AlertDialogCancel,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
} from '~/components/alert-dialog'
import { Button, buttonVariants } from '~/components/button'
import { Input } from '~/components/input'
import { Label } from '~/components/label'
import * as React from 'react'

const PROJECT = 'duck-pond'

export function Demo() {
  const field = React.useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null)
  const [typed, setTyped] = React.useState('')

  return (
    <AlertDialog onOpenChange={() => setTyped('')}>
      <AlertDialogTrigger asChild>
        <Button variant="destructive">Delete project</Button>
      </AlertDialogTrigger>
      <AlertDialogContent initialFocus={field}>
        <AlertDialogHeader>
          <AlertDialogTitle>Delete {PROJECT}?</AlertDialogTitle>
          <AlertDialogDescription>
            This removes the project and its deployments. Type its name to confirm.
          </AlertDialogDescription>
        </AlertDialogHeader>
        <div className="grid gap-2">
          <Label htmlFor="project-name">Project name</Label>
          <Input
            autoComplete="off"
            id="project-name"
            onChange={(event) => setTyped(event.target.value)}
            placeholder={PROJECT}
            ref={field}
            value={typed}
          />
        </div>
        <AlertDialogFooter>
          <AlertDialogCancel>Cancel</AlertDialogCancel>
          <AlertDialogAction className={buttonVariants({ variant: 'destructive' })} disabled={typed !== PROJECT}>
            Delete
          </AlertDialogAction>
        </AlertDialogFooter>
      </AlertDialogContent>
    </AlertDialog>
  )
}

import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogAction,
  AlertDialogCancel,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
} from '~/components/alert-dialog'
import { Button, buttonVariants } from '~/components/button'
import * as React from 'react'

const deleteProject = () => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1200))

export function Demo() {
  const [open, setOpen] = React.useState(false)
  const [deleting, setDeleting] = React.useState(false)

  return (
    <AlertDialog open={open} onOpenChange={(next) => !deleting && setOpen(next)}>
      <AlertDialogTrigger asChild>
        <Button variant="destructive">Delete project</Button>
      </AlertDialogTrigger>
      <AlertDialogContent>
        <AlertDialogHeader>
          <AlertDialogTitle>Delete the project?</AlertDialogTitle>
          <AlertDialogDescription>The dialog stays open until the project is gone.</AlertDialogDescription>
        </AlertDialogHeader>
        <AlertDialogFooter>
          <AlertDialogCancel disabled={deleting}>Cancel</AlertDialogCancel>
          <AlertDialogAction
            className={buttonVariants({ variant: 'destructive' })}
            disabled={deleting}
            onClick={async (event) => {
              event.preventDefault()
              setDeleting(true)
              await deleteProject()
              setDeleting(false)
              setOpen(false)
            }}>
            {deleting ? 'Deleting...' : 'Delete'}
          </AlertDialogAction>
        </AlertDialogFooter>
      </AlertDialogContent>
    </AlertDialog>
  )
}

Rather than shipping a monolithic DataTable component with 50 props, we teach you to build tables progressively using TanStack Table primitives. Each feature - sorting, filtering, pagination, selection - layers on independently. You only pay for what you use. ## Introduction Every data table or datagrid I've created has been unique. They all behave differently, have specific sorting and filtering requirements, and work with different data sources. It doesn't make sense to combine all of these variations into a single component. If we do that, we'll lose the flexibility that [headless UI](https://tanstack.com/table/v8/docs/introduction#what-is-headless-ui) provides. So instead of a data-table component, I thought it would be more helpful to provide a guide on how to build your own. AspectRatio solves the CSS aspect-ratio problem with a clean component API, preventing layout shifts when images and videos load. The `ratio` prop is the only knob you need - everything else is handled by the container's CSS. ## How It's Built primitives["@gentleduck/primitives\n/slot"]:::internal AspectRatio --> libs["@gentleduck/libs"]:::internal primitives --> |"provides"| SlotRendering["Slot Rendering\n(wraps child)"] AspectRatio --> |"manages"| PaddingTrick["CSS Padding\nAspect Ratio"] AspectRatio --> |"adds"| ResponsiveMedia["Responsive Media\nContainment"] classDef internal fill:#2dd4bf,stroke:#14b8a6,color:#fff `} /> ## Installation CLI Manual ```bash npx @gentleduck/cli add aspect-ratio ``` Install the following dependencies: ```bash npm install @gentleduck/primitives @gentleduck/libs ``` Copy and paste the following code into your project. ```tsx // aspect-ratio.tsx 'use client' import { cn } from '@gentleduck/libs/cn' import { useDirection } from '@gentleduck/primitives/direction' import { Slot } from '@gentleduck/primitives/slot' import React from 'react' import { toDirection } from '../direction/direction.libs' const AspectRatio = React.forwardRef< React.ComponentRef, React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef & { ratio: string } >(({ style, className, ratio, dir, ...props }, ref) => { const direction = useDirection(toDirection(dir)) return ( ) }) AspectRatio.displayName = 'AspectRatio' export { AspectRatio } ``` ```typescript // index.ts export { AspectRatio } from './aspect-ratio' export { MotionAspectRatio } from './motion-aspect-ratio' ``` ```tsx // motion-aspect-ratio.tsx 'use client' import { scaleIn } from '@gentleduck/motion/presets/scale-in' import { springBouncy } from '@gentleduck/motion/transitions/springs' import { withMotion } from '../_internal/motion-shell' import { AspectRatio } from './aspect-ratio' const MotionAspectRatio = withMotion(AspectRatio, scaleIn, { transition: springBouncy }, undefined) MotionAspectRatio.displayName = 'MotionAspectRatio' export { MotionAspectRatio } ``` Update the import paths to match your project setup. ## Usage ```tsx import Image from "next/image" import { AspectRatio } from "@/components/ui/aspect-ratio" ``` ```tsx
``` ## RTL Support Set the direction once with `DirectionProvider` (or ``) and the aspect ratio follows it. No `dir` prop or `rtl:` classes needed. ```tsx import { AspectRatio } from '~/components/aspect-ratio' import { DirectionProvider } from '~/components/direction' import Image from 'next/image' export function Demo() { return ( ) } ``` ## Motion } title="Alpha: Motion Compositions" tone="warning"> Motion components work standalone, but some compositions may behave unexpectedly: this is still under active development. If you find a broken composition, please [file an issue](https://github.com/gentleeduck/gentleduck/issues). Use `MotionAspectRatio` for a smooth scale + blur entrance animation powered by [motion](https://motion.dev). The content scales from 0.95 and unblurs on mount. ```tsx 'use client' import { MotionAspectRatio } from '~/components/aspect-ratio' import Image from 'next/image' export function Demo() { return ( ) } ``` }> Requires the `motion` package. Note: `MotionAspectRatio` adds an animated `div` wrapper around `AspectRatio`; the inner `Slot`/`asChild` behavior is unchanged. ## API Reference ### AspectRatio | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `dir` | `'ltr' \| 'rtl'` | - | Text direction override. Resolved via `useDirection` (`dir` prop -> `DirectionProvider` -> ``). | | `ratio` | `number` | (required) | Aspect ratio of the container, e.g. `16/9`, `4/3` | | `className` | `string` | `--` | Additional class names to apply to the container | | `style` | `React.CSSProperties` | `--` | Inline styles applied to the container (aspect-ratio is merged automatically) | | `children` | `React.ReactNode` | `--` | Child element to render inside the aspect-ratio container | | `...props` | `React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef` | - | Additional props inherited from `Slot`. | *Uses a `Slot` wrapper, so the child element receives the aspect-ratio styles.* ### MotionAspectRatio Wraps `AspectRatio` in an animated `div` that scales from 0.95 with 8px blur fade on mount, using the `scaleIn` preset and a bouncy spring transition (stiffness 500, damping 28). The wrapped `AspectRatio` still renders its child via `Slot` internally.     Shipping a release

    Every element below is what a markdown renderer writes. Press Ctrl + K to search, and read the CHANGELOG first. The build takes about two minutes. Lookups take log 2 n steps, and the cache holds 104 entries.

    Steps

    1. Bump the version
      • Patch for fixes
      • Minor for features
    2. Tag the commit

    Checklist

    • Tests pass
    • Docs updated

    Terms

    Changeset
    A file naming the packages a change bumps, and by how much.
    What if the build fails?

    Fix it on a branch and tag again. A failed build publishes nothing.
